title: Fast-forwarding quantum algorithms for weakly nonlinear dissipative differential equations and beyond
abstract: We study a fast-forwarded quantum algorithm for solving weakly nonlinear dissipative ordinary differential equations. Our approach is a combination of the Carleman embedding technique and the linear combination of Hamiltonian simulation algorithm for linearized systems with fast-forwarded scaling. The complexity of our algorithm does not explicitly depend on the evolution time $T$, thus greatly improving the previous state-of-the-art $\widetilde{\mathcal{O}}(\sqrt{T})$ to $\mathcal{O}(1)$, and any remaining time dependence enters through the output norm and forcing parameters. We rigorously analyze the performance of this approach by convergence guarantees of the Carleman embedding for time-dependent coefficient matrices and detailed complexity estimates, and improve the realization of the Carleman-embedding-based algorithms by simplifying the post-selection step. In addition, we perform a numerical study on differential equations beyond the weakly nonlinear case, and identify possibility of achieving fast-forwarding scaling for systems with stronger nonlinearity or linear non-resonant effect.
summary: This paper introduces a fast-forwarded quantum algorithm to solve weakly nonlinear dissipative ODEs, achieving a time-independent complexity scaling. It achieves this by linearizing the nonlinear system using the Carleman embedding technique and applying advanced quantum simulation methods. This breakthrough significantly improves the feasibility of simulating complex, dissipative physical processes on quantum hardware.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of efficiently simulating the time evolution governed by weakly nonlinear dissipative ordinary differential equations (ODEs) using quantum computation.
main_result: A novel fast-forwarded quantum algorithm is proposed that achieves a computational complexity explicitly independent of the evolution time T, significantly improving upon previous scaling bounds.
method: The approach combines the Carleman embedding technique to linearize the nonlinear ODEs with a fast-forwarded quantum linear ODE solver, leveraging the dissipativity of the linearized system.
model_or_system: The focus is on solving general weakly nonlinear dissipative ODEs, exemplified by quadratic nonlinear forms. The core technique involves transforming the nonlinear system into a high-dimensional, linear, dissipative system via Carleman embedding.

important_parameters: The dissipativity condition ($\mu(F_1) < 0$) and the weak nonlinearity condition ($R < 1$) are crucial for the algorithm's convergence and complexity bounds.
main_assumptions: The primary fast-forwarding algorithm requires the linear part of the ODE to be dissipative. Alternative contour-integral methods are restricted to time-independent coefficients.

paper_structure: The paper builds from establishing the physical problem (nonlinear ODEs) to the mathematical tool (Carleman embedding for linearization), then develops the quantum algorithm (combining LCHS with fast-forwarding), and finally analyzes the error bounds and limitations.
why_interesting: This work provides a concrete, complexity-improving quantum algorithm for simulating open quantum systems described by dissipative dynamics, which is a major challenge in quantum simulation.

Figure 1 shows the decay of the error EN as N increases. One observes that, for all tested parameter choices, the truncation error decreases monotonically with respect to the Carleman truncation order. In particular, for the cases with R < 1, the convergence is very rapid. The error drops by several orders of magnitude as N increases from 1 to 10. This is fully consistent with the theoretical prediction. More interestingly, the cases with R > 1 also exhibit clear numerical convergence. In particular, even when R ≈1.01, 1.16, or 1.57, the error still decreases as N grows, although the decay rate becomes significantly slower than in the cases with R < 1.
